assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the working core of modern monetary policy analysis. It combines staggered-price microfoundations, an interest-rate rule for policy and a coherent welfare-based synthesis. It has had very large influence on central-bank practice and on macroeconomic theory, and it is a field-defining contribution.
assessment.attribution: Calvo is credited with the staggered-pricing device, Taylor with the policy rule and its empirical and policy use, and Woodford with the integrated microfounded synthesis. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets also made major contributions (Gali and Gertler on the Phillips curve, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets on estimated DSGE models). A three-person limit forces a judgment on whom to credit. The 2022 prize to Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig is adjacent but covers banking and financial crises, not nominal rigidities.
assessment.maturity: The core contributions date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and have been tested through several decades of policy use, including the post-2008 and post-pandemic inflation episodes.
uncertainties: Who should be credited among a large group of contributors.
Criticism of the framework after the 2008 crisis and the 2021-23 inflation, and the rise of heterogeneous-agent alternatives.
Whether the Committee would see recent monetary-policy prizes as reducing the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work shows how technology, tasks and import competition reshape labour demand, wages and local labour markets. It changed how economists and policymakers think about wage inequality and trade adjustment, and it is empirically rigorous and widely cited.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz are central to the task-based and skill-biased view of technology. Autor, Dorn and Hanson are central to the China-shock evidence. Dorn is a clear co-author on the trade-shock work, and Acemoglu's task-framework contributions were recognised in 2024. Choosing Autor, Hanson and Katz is a defensible but contestable allocation.
assessment.maturity: The task literature dates from the early 2000s and the China-shock papers from about 2013. There is now more than a decade of replication, extension and debate.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and persistence of the China shock, and over identification choices.
Overlap with the 2021 and 2023 labour prizes and the 2024 technology and institutions prize.
Attribution among Dorn, Hanson, Autor and Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This line of work links optimal tax theory to empirical elasticities through sufficient-statistics methods, and has changed how tax policy is evaluated. It rests on strong evidence and has a direct policy role.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod is a pioneer of taxable-income behavioural responses. Saez combines the theory and the evidence on top incomes and optimal taxation. Chetty advanced sufficient-statistics and quasi-experimental methods. Stantcheva is clearly important but earlier in her career, so crediting her is less likely to be considered mature. Saez and Chetty also appear on other ballots, which blurs attribution across candidates.
assessment.maturity: Taxable-income elasticity work dates from the 1990s and 2000s, and the optimal-tax and sufficient-statistics work from the 2000s and 2010s. The empirical conclusions are still under active testing.
uncertainties: Overlap of laureate names with the inequality and mobility candidates, which makes a combined award possible.
Sensitivity of elasticity estimates to identification and to tax-avoidance margins.
Whether Chetty's work is better credited under the mobility candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification and moment inequalities give a principled way to do inference when strong assumptions are not credible. This is a fundamental methodological contribution that clarifies the role of assumptions in empirical work and is used in applied microeconomics and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Manski founded the field with the bounds approach and the identification problem. Tamer and Molinari developed the econometric inference methods and applications. Manski has the clearest priority, and the others are plausible co-recipients, though Chernozhukov, Imbens and others also contributed to inference in this area.
assessment.maturity: Manski's foundational work dates from the late 1980s and 1990s. The inference theory and applications of the 2000s and 2010s are well developed. The 2021 prize recognised adjacent causal-inference work.
uncertainties: Adoption in applied work is narrower than for design-based methods.
Overlap with the 2021 causal-inference prize.
Who among the inference-theory contributors should share credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity trade models changed trade theory and empirics, by explaining within-industry reallocation, exporter selection and a new channel for gains from trade. They are broadly used in the field and in policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 model is the central contribution. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple and related work, plus Helpman's broader trade-theory legacy, support Helpman. Redding is credited in the list but is more naturally associated with quantitative spatial and trade models. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are important contributors who are not on this ballot's list.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are from 2003 to 2008, so the work has had about two decades of application, though it is a variation on the 2008 trade prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2008 prize for new trade theory and with the Helpman-Grossman political-economy ballot.
Omitted contributors outside the credited names.
Size of the quantitative gains in practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law and finance literature put legal institutions and investor protection at the centre of comparative finance and development, and it has been very influential. It sits alongside the 2024 institutions prize, though with a different emphasis.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny jointly produced the foundational papers. Shleifer has a wide independent body of work in behavioural finance and corporate governance, so the credited set is a plausible but not unique selection of three.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers are from 1997 to 1998 and have had a long period of replication. Several of their empirical claims have also been challenged over time.
uncertainties: Serious critiques of the legal-origins hypothesis, including measurement and causal-identification objections.
Overlap with the 2024 prize and the difficulty of choosing three from four.
Possible reputational or other concerns that are outside the evidence provided.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are an enabling tool used in a large share of applied micro and growth work. The contribution is methodological but widely adopted, and its practical effect is large.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond (1991), Arellano and Bover and Blundell and Bond (1998) are the key papers. Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen, and Anderson and Hsiao, are important antecedents, so the credited set omits some prior work. Blundell has contributions in labour and public economics that help his case.
assessment.maturity: The main work is from 1991 to 1998, and has been well tested and widely implemented in software.
uncertainties: Weak-instrument and proliferation problems in applied use of these estimators.
Whether the Committee prefers a tool contribution to a conceptual advance.
Prior contributions that complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a new area of information economics, with a tractable framework for how a sender's choice of information structure shapes decisions. It has applications in markets, regulation, and platforms and ties into earlier mechanism-design theory.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated the persuasion model. Bergemann and Morris developed information design and the Bayes correlated equilibrium, and Morris's earlier work on global games and robust mechanism design adds to the case. Choosing three of four requires a contested decision between the two strands.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from about 2011 to 2019, so the field is younger and its empirical and applied reach is still being established.
uncertainties: Relatively recent origin and limited empirical validation.
Division of credit between the persuasion and information-design strands.
Overlap with the earlier information-economics prizes (1996, 2001, 2007).
